Following administration of pain relief, you consider further imaging options to evaluate Anna’s potential spinal injuries fully. As part of the initial primary survey, a lateral c-spine, chest and pelvic film were performed in the resuscitation bay.

Is the lateral c-spine radiograph alone adequate to rule out a fracture?
explanation: A lateral cervical spine film alone is not sufficient to exclude cervical spine fracture in a child with significant mechanism and neck pain. A complete assessment usually requires adequate multi-view imaging and, if suspicion remains or films are inadequate, further imaging such as CT/MRI depending on the clinical context.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Trauma 2 - Pain

rationale: The question tests initial imaging of possible paediatric cervical spine injury. Because the child has a significant fall and symptoms suggestive of spinal injury, a single lateral c-spine view is not enough to exclude fracture.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect. A single lateral view can miss important cervical spine injuries.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. One lateral c-spine radiograph does not reliably rule out fracture.

Clinical scenario 3 - Anna

The following eight questions refer to Anna’s clinical scenario.

Teaching/learning points:

Immobilisation in children

Anatomical differences

SCIWORA

The triage nurse rushes into resuscitation with nine year old Anna and her parents. Anna is in her father’s arms. She has fallen from their first-floor balcony onto the lawn below. Her fall was not witnessed but heard by her parents, who immediately found her on her back in the garden crying. Rather than calling an ambulance, Anna’s parents brought her to emergency in their car.

The triage nurse is concerned Anna has fallen a significant height (greater than twice her standing height). Anna initially appears alert and very distressed. She is complaining of severe neck and back pain. Her respiratory rate is 26/min, saturations 100% in air, heart rate 110bpm, blood pressure 100/60. Based on her mechanism of injury, Anna was immediately secured on a spinal board with three straps, a hard cervical collar and sandbags.
